facts.text: Pratts emerged as a distinct crossroads community in the 1740s, named after the Pratt family, early English settlers.
The community sits at 38°20′51″N 78°16′12″W, about 590 feet above sea level in Virginia’s Piedmont.
SR 230 and SR 231 run concurrently on Orange Road to the center of Pratts, where SR 231 turns south onto Blue Ridge Turnpike.
A VDOT project plans a roundabout at the Routes 230/231 intersection to improve safety, with a public hearing in August 2025.
Pratts lies about 2.4 miles southwest of Madison and 90 miles southwest of Washington, D.C., placing it in a rural setting near the Blue Ridge Mountains.
The climate is humid subtropical, with warm humid summers averaging 85°F in July and cold winters averaging 23°F in January, sometimes snowing due to nearby Blue Ridge.
